title: Equal Groups: Multiplication
seo_title: Multiplication Class 4 Worksheet with Answers (Maths Mela Chapter 9)
standard_code: Class 4, Maths Mela Chapter 9: Equal Groups
standard_text: Multiplication: equal groups and arrays, multiplication facts, multiplying 2- and 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 4)
meta_desc: Class 4 Equal Groups worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 9): times tables, factor pairs, multiplying by 10 and short multiplication. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Multiplying by 10 moves the digits one place left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Know the tables to 10 × 10.
  • Split numbers: 6 × 34 = 6 × 30 + 6 × 4 = 180 + 24 = 204.
  • × 10: 37 → 370; × 100: 37 → 3,700.

Examples

Example

7 × 46

7 × 40 = 280

7 × 6 = 42

280 + 42

Answer: 322

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying only the tensMultiply both the tens and the ones.
Forgetting the carried tenAdd it to the next column.

faq.q: Which tables should Class 4 children know?

faq.a: Two numbers that multiply to make a number, like 4 and 6 for 24.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: 6 rows with 4 dots in each row: 6 × 4 = 24.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: 3 rows with 7 dots in each row: 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: 2 rows with 9 dots in each row: 2 × 9 = 18.

items.q: How many dots are in this array?
items.e: 4 rows with 8 dots in each row: 4 × 8 = 32.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 5 rows with 3 dots in each row, so it shows 5 × 3 = 15. 3 × 5 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 3 rows with 6 dots in each row, so it shows 3 × 6 = 18. 6 × 3 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 4 rows with 7 dots in each row, so it shows 4 × 7 = 28. 7 × 4 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.

items.q: Which multiplication matches this array?
items.e: There are 2 rows with 8 dots in each row, so it shows 2 × 8 = 16. 8 × 2 gives the same answer: it is the array turned on its side.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 8 × 10 = 80.
10 × 5 = 50. Take away one 5: 50 − 5 = 45. Check: the digits add up to 9.
10 × 12 = 120. Take away one 12: 120 − 12 = 108. Check: the digits add up to 9.

items.q: What is 36 × 10?
items.e: × 10 moves every digit one place to the left: 3 tens become 3 hundreds and 6 ones become 6 tens. A 0 holds the ones place. 36 × 10 = 360.

items.q: What is 100 × 8?
items.e: × 100 moves the digit two places to the left: 8 ones become 8 hundreds. 100 × 8 = 800.

items.q: What is 45 × 100?
items.e: × 100 moves both digits two places to the left: 45 × 100 = 4,500. 450 is only × 10.

items.q: What is 10 × 70?
items.e: 70 is 7 tens. 10 × 7 tens = 70 tens = 700.

items.q: What is 420 ÷ 10?
items.e: ÷ 10 moves every digit one place to the right: 4 hundreds become 4 tens and 2 tens become 2 ones. 420 ÷ 10 = 42.
÷ 100 moves every digit two places to the right: 3,500 ÷ 100 = 35. 350 is only ÷ 10.

items.q: You know that 6 × 7 = 42. What is 60 × 7?
items.e: Use the fact 6 × 7. 60 is 6 tens, so the answer is 42 tens: 60 × 7 = 420.

items.q: You know that 8 × 3 = 24. What is 8 × 300?
items.e: Use the fact 8 × 3. 300 is 3 hundreds, so the answer is 24 hundreds: 8 × 300 = 2,400.

items.q: You know that 9 × 4 = 36. What is 9 × 40?
items.e: Use the fact 9 × 4. 40 is 4 tens, so the answer is 36 tens: 9 × 40 = 360.

items.q: You know that 12 × 5 = 60. What is 12 × 50?
items.e: Use the fact 12 × 5. 50 is 5 tens, so the answer is 60 tens: 12 × 50 = 600.

items.q: What is 70 × 8?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56. 70 is 7 tens, so 70 × 8 = 56 tens = 560. (78 comes from adding.)

items.q: You know that 42 ÷ 7 = 6. What is 420 ÷ 7?
items.e: 420 is 42 tens. 42 tens ÷ 7 = 6 tens = 60. Check: 60 × 7 = 420.

items.q: What is 360 ÷ 9?
What is 480 ÷ 6?
You know that 27 ÷ 9 = 3. What is 2,700 ÷ 9?
items.e: 2,700 is 27 hundreds. 27 hundreds ÷ 9 = 3 hundreds = 300. Check: 300 × 9 = 2,700.

items.q: Find the missing number: ? × 8 = 560
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, and 560 is 56 tens. So the missing number is 7 tens = 70. Check: 70 × 8 = 560.

items.q: Find the missing number: 30 × ? = 270
items.e: 30 is 3 tens and 270 is 27 tens. 3 × 9 = 27, so the missing number is 9. Check: 30 × 9 = 270.

items.q: Find the missing number: 400 ÷ ? = 80
items.e: 8 × 5 = 40, so 80 × 5 = 400. The missing number is 5. Check: 400 ÷ 5 = 80.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 50 × 9?
Which fact helps you work out 630 ÷ 7?
24 counters are in 3 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 3 × ? = 24
items.e: Count the counters in one row: 8. 3 × 8 = 24, so 3 and 8 are a factor pair of 24.
Count the counters in one row: 9. 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 and 9 are a factor pair of 36.

items.q: 18 counters are in 2 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 2 × ? = 18
items.e: Count the counters in one row: 9. 2 × 9 = 18, so 2 and 9 are a factor pair of 18.

items.q: 30 counters are in 5 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 5 × ? = 30
items.e: Count the counters in one row: 6. 5 × 6 = 30, so 5 and 6 are a factor pair of 30.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 36?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36. 16 + 20 also makes 36, but a factor pair must multiply to make 36.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 40?
items.e: 5 × 8 = 40. 20 + 20 also makes 40, but a factor pair must multiply to make 40.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 56?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56. 50 + 6 also makes 56, but a factor pair must multiply to make 56.

items.q: Which is not a factor pair of 24?
items.e: 6 × 3 = 18, not 24. The others are factor pairs: 1 × 24 = 24, 2 × 12 = 24, 3 × 8 = 24.

items.q: Which is not a factor pair of 36?
items.e: 8 × 4 = 32, not 36. The others are factor pairs: 2 × 18 = 36, 3 × 12 = 36, 4 × 9 = 36.

items.q: Which is not a factor pair of 48?
items.e: 6 × 9 = 54, not 48. The others are factor pairs: 6 × 8 = 48, 4 × 12 = 48, 3 × 16 = 48.

items.q: Fatima lists the factor pairs of 24: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 4 × 6. Which pair did she miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 3 × 8 = 24 is missing. Swapping a pair (like 6 × 4) does not make a new pair.

items.q: Harsh lists the factor pairs of 30: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 5 × 6. Which pair did he miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 3 × 10 = 30 is missing. Swapping a pair (like 6 × 5) does not make a new pair.

items.q: Lakshmi lists the factor pairs of 36: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 6 × 6. Which pair did she miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 4 × 9 = 36 is missing. Swapping a pair (like 12 × 3) does not make a new pair.

items.q: How many factor pairs does 18 have?
items.e: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. That is 3 pairs. 1 × 18 counts too.

items.q: How many factor pairs does 16 have?
items.e: 1 × 16, 2 × 8, 4 × 4. That is 3 pairs. Count 4 × 4 only once.

items.q: Use the factor pair 12 = 6 × 2. What is 12 × 5?
items.e: 12 × 5 = 6 × 2 × 5 = 6 × 10 = 60. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Use the factor pair 14 = 7 × 2. What is 14 × 5?
items.e: 14 × 5 = 7 × 2 × 5 = 7 × 10 = 70. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Use the factor pair 6 = 2 × 3. What is 15 × 6?
items.e: 15 × 6 = 15 × 2 × 3 = 30 × 3 = 90. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Use the factor pair 8 = 4 × 2. What is 25 × 8?
items.e: 25 × 8 = 25 × 4 × 2 = 100 × 2 = 200. Remember to use every factor.

items.q: Which calculation helps you work out 16 × 5?
items.e: 8 × 2 = 16, so 16 × 5 = 8 × 2 × 5 = 8 × 10 = 80. Splitting 16 into its digits does not work: 1 × 6 = 6, not 16. And 8 × 8 = 64, not 16.

items.q: Use the grid method to find 67 × 5.
What number goes in the box marked ?
items.e: The ? box is 60 × 8. 6 × 8 = 48, so 6 tens × 8 = 48 tens = 480. The whole grid: 65 × 8 = 480 + 40 = 520.

items.q: What number goes in the box marked ?
items.e: The ? box is 80 × 7. 8 × 7 = 56, so 8 tens × 7 = 56 tens = 560. The whole grid: 87 × 7 = 560 + 49 = 609.

items.q: Which is the same as 34 × 5?
items.e: Partition 34 into 30 + 4. Multiply both parts by 5, then add: 30 × 5 + 4 × 5 = 150 + 20 = 170.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 25 × 7 = ☐ × 7 + 5 × 7
items.e: 25 = 20 + 5, so 25 × 7 = 20 × 7 + 5 × 7. The missing number is 20 (2 tens, not 2).

items.q: Use the grid method to find 67 × 3.
Use the grid method to find 87 × 9.
Which is the same as 75 × 6?
items.e: Partition 75 into 70 + 5. Multiply both parts by 6, then add: 70 × 6 + 5 × 6 = 420 + 30 = 450.

items.q: What number goes in the box marked ?
items.e: The ? box is 2 × 7 = 14. The whole grid: 32 × 7 = 210 + 14 = 224.

items.q: Use the grid method to find 12 × 9.
Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 2 × 4 = 8. Tens: 1 × 4 = 4. Multiply both digits. Answer: 48.

items.q: Start with the ones: 4 × 7 = 28. What do you do?
items.e: 28 ones = 2 tens and 8 ones. Write 8 in the ones column. Exchange 2 tens: write a small 2 under the tens column. Ones: 4 × 7 = 28. Write 8, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 3 × 7 + 2 = 23. Write 23. Answer: 238.

items.q: What is 87 × 9?
items.e: Ones: 7 × 9 = 63. Write 3, exchange 6 tens. Tens: 8 × 9 + 6 = 78. Write 78. Answer: 783.

items.q: What is 49 × 6?
items.e: Ones: 9 × 6 = 54. Write 4, exchange 5 tens. Tens: 4 × 6 + 5 = 29. Write 29. Answer: 294.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 8 × 4 = 32. Write 2, exchange 3 tens. Tens: 5 × 4 + 3 = 23. Write 23. Answer: 232.

items.q: Start with the ones: 2 × 7 = 14. What do you do?
items.e: 14 ones = 1 ten and 4 ones. Write 4 in the ones column. Exchange 1 ten: write a small 1 under the tens column. Ones: 2 × 7 = 14. Write 4, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 8 × 7 + 1 = 57. Write 57. Answer: 574.

items.q: What is 42 × 2?
items.e: Ones: 2 × 2 = 4. Tens: 4 × 2 = 8. Multiply both digits. Answer: 84.

items.q: What is 46 × 6?
items.e: Ones: 6 × 6 = 36. Write 6, exchange 3 tens. Tens: 4 × 6 + 3 = 27. Write 27. Answer: 276.

items.q: Use short multiplication.
items.e: Ones: 9 × 4 = 36. Write 6, exchange 3 tens. Tens: 1 × 4 + 3 = 7. Write 7. Answer: 76.

items.q: What is 12 × 5?
items.e: Ones: 2 × 5 = 10. Write 0, exchange 1 ten. Tens: 1 × 5 + 1 = 6. Write 6. Answer: 60.

items.q: Eggs come in boxes of 12. Tara buys 7 boxes for the school cake sale. How many eggs is that?
items.e: 7 boxes of 12: 12 × 7 = 70 + 14 = 84. 72 is only 6 boxes.

items.q: There are 11 players in a football team. How many players are in 6 teams?
items.e: 6 teams of 11: 11 × 6 = 66. Write the 6 twice.

items.q: How many days are there in 9 weeks?
items.e: There are 7 days in a week. 9 × 7 = 63. 56 is only 8 weeks.

items.q: Crisps come in multipacks of 6. Harsh buys 9 multipacks for a class party. How many bags of crisps does he get?
items.e: 9 packs of 6: 9 × 6 = 54. 45 has the digits the wrong way round.

items.q: A spider has 8 legs. Isha finds 7 spiders in the garden. How many legs is that altogether?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56. Double 7 three times: 14, 28, 56.

items.q: 48 students get into teams of 6 for PE. How many teams are there?
items.e: 48 ÷ 6 = ? Think 6 × ? = 48. 6 × 8 = 48, so there are 8 teams.

items.q: A minibus holds 12 children. How many minibuses are needed for 96 children on a school trip?
items.e: 96 ÷ 12 = ? 12 × 8 = 96, so 8 minibuses are full with no one left behind.

items.q: In the school hall, there are 11 rows of chairs with 9 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
items.e: 11 × 9 = 99. Write the 9 twice.

items.q: How many weeks are there in 84 days?
items.e: There are 7 days in a week. 84 ÷ 7 = ? 7 × 12 = 84, so 12 weeks.

items.q: There are 12 months in a year. How many months are there in 5 years?
Ananya’s book has 168 pages. A dictionary has 6 times as many pages. How many pages does the dictionary have?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 6 × 168 pages. Ones: 8 × 6 = 48. Write 8, exchange 4 tens. Tens: 6 × 6 + 4 = 40. Write 0, exchange 4 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 6 + 4 = 10. Write 10. Answer: 1,008. So the answer is 1,008 pages.

items.q: The school hall has 9 rows of chairs with 23 chairs in each row. How many chairs are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 9 × 23 chairs. Ones: 3 × 9 = 27. Write 7, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 2 × 9 + 2 = 20. Write 20. Answer: 207. So the answer is 207 chairs.

items.q: A swimming pool is 25 m long. Shreya swims 8 lengths. How far does she swim?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 8 × 25 m. Ones: 5 × 8 = 40. Write 0, exchange 4 tens. Tens: 2 × 8 + 4 = 20. Write 20. Answer: 200. So the answer is 200 m.

items.q: Isha walks 875 m to school. How far does she walk to school in 5 days?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 5 × 875 m. Ones: 5 × 5 = 25. Write 5, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 7 × 5 + 2 = 37. Write 7, exchange 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 8 × 5 + 3 = 43. Write 43. Answer: 4,375. So the answer is 4,375 m.

items.q: A school has 6 boxes of 144 pencils. It gives out 500 pencils. How many pencils are left?
items.e: Step 1: pencils: 6 × 144 = 864 (4 × 6 = 24, write 4, exchange 2; 4 × 6 + 2 = 26, write 6, exchange 2; 1 × 6 + 2 = 8). Step 2: 864 − 500 = 364.

items.q: A packet has 18 biscuits. The teacher buys 7 packets for the school fair. How many biscuits is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 7 × 18 biscuits. Ones: 8 × 7 = 56. Write 6, exchange 5 tens. Tens: 1 × 7 + 5 = 12. Write 12. Answer: 126. So the answer is 126 biscuits.

items.q: A box holds 144 pencils. The school orders 6 boxes. How many pencils is that?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 6 × 144 pencils. Ones: 4 × 6 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 4 × 6 + 2 = 26. Write 6, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 6 + 2 = 8. Write 8. Answer: 864. So the answer is 864 pencils.

items.q: A school books 4 coaches with 54 seats each. 187 people go on the trip. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Step 1: seats: 4 × 54 = 216 (4 × 4 = 16, write 6, exchange 1; 5 × 4 + 1 = 21). Step 2: empty seats: 216 − 187 = 29.

items.q: There are 28 children in each class. The juniors have 7 classes. How many junior children are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 7 × 28 children. Ones: 8 × 7 = 56. Write 6, exchange 5 tens. Tens: 2 × 7 + 5 = 19. Write 19. Answer: 196. So the answer is 196 children.

items.q: A train has 6 carriages. Each carriage has 74 seats. How many seats are on the train?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 6 × 74 seats. Ones: 4 × 6 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 7 × 6 + 2 = 44. Write 44. Answer: 444. So the answer is 444 seats.
